install-kube-agents.summary: Lets a repo-level or operator-facing agent install kube-agents onto a GKE cluster in a GCP project by driving install.sh non-interactively: detect the environment with gcloud, interview the operator for project, region, cluster, model provider, chat channel and permission set, run --dry-run or --generate-only, then apply through terraform/examples/full-install/lifecycle.sh and the Helm chart. Covers adopting an existing cluster (Workload Identity, CMEK, node-pool migration, NetworkPolicy consent flags), the GitHub token minter setup for GitOps pull requests, the JSON status report, the terminal handover for a chat-less install, and the full install.sh flag table. It is a write skill against GCP and one host cluster; it explicitly hands upgrades to upgrade-kube-agents, never asks for secrets in chat, and never passes adoption flags without operator consent.

review-address-feedback.summary: Guides a repo contributor agent through one review round on an open kube-agents pull request: collect unresolved threads, review-body findings and red checks, cross-check them against the Self-Review section, triage each as fix, push-back or deferral, bracket fixes with red/green evidence, fix the whole class, re-review with review-preflight, push once, reply in every thread with proof, request one re-read, and resolve settled threads once the re-read lands. It is GitHub-side, write-to-branch work for the author of the PR, with no cluster access involved. It defers the commands to docs/pull-request-workflow.md and the rules to AGENTS.md, and states no other exclusions.

review-adversarial.summary: Gives a reviewing agent the method for a hostile read of a diff range in this repo: fix the range with a three-dot diff, state the change's intent, hunt candidates from ten named angles (line scan, removed behaviour, cross-file tracing, operations and security, reuse, simplification, altitude, conventions and docs, scope and test coverage, sibling pull requests), re-derive every candidate from source into CONFIRMED, PLAUSIBLE or REFUTED, then record a fixed or deliberately-not-fixed disposition per survivor with BLOCKER/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW severity. It is read-only on the repo apart from step 6 (edit on CONFIRMED) and is used by authors before a PR, by reviewers through pr-review-batch, and by kube-agents-bot as its playbook. It explicitly excludes the full documentation-drift question (left to review-docs-drift) and all plumbing such as spawning the clean context (left to review-preflight).

review-docs-drift.summary: Lets a repo contributor or reviewer agent check a branch diff against main for documentation drift in both directions: which docs a code change should have updated (generated regions, identifier sources, prose pages), and whether changed docs still match source, the canonical-home table in AGENTS.md, the docs/README.md map, and the site audience rule. It names git diff and git grep steps, the make docs-check, make docs-generate, prettier and site build gates, and reports a Blocking/Advisory triage table. It is read-only by design (the report is the deliverable, no silent fixes) and holds no repository facts of its own; it does not cover code defects, which it leaves to review-adversarial.

review-preflight.summary: Plumbing for the author of a kube-agents branch before opening a pull request: fetch and fix the base diff range, run make docs-check in the main loop, spawn one subagent each for review-adversarial and review-docs-drift (or a fresh headless session when subagents are unavailable), hand each only the repo, range, skill path and gate output while withholding intent and commit messages, then merge the returned findings into one severity-ordered disposition list that becomes the PR's Self-Review section. It covers re-runs after fixes and what to do when no clean context can be obtained. It explicitly holds no review method of its own and does not restate the requirement, which AGENTS.md owns.

review-security-k8s-admission.summary: A short checklist for a repo-level security reviewer auditing Kubernetes admission control manifests: ValidatingWebhookConfiguration, MutatingWebhookConfiguration, ValidatingAdmissionPolicy and MutatingAdmissionPolicy. It covers failurePolicy and timeouts, namespaceSelector/objectSelector exemptions, binding scope, CEL failure handling and message leakage, caBundle/HTTPS and NetworkPolicy ingress to the webhook, and mutating risks such as sidecar injection, reinvocationPolicy, CEL side effects and execution order. It is read-only review guidance applicable to any cluster or manifest, part of the review-security-k8s-* family; it does not state exclusions.

review-security-k8s-agents-audit-logs.summary: A repo-level review skill for a contributor or review agent, run as a sub-agent of review-security-k8s-agents-main. It is a read-only checklist applied to manifests and agent configs: one dedicated ServiceAccount per agent, an API audit policy that captures agent requests at Metadata or RequestResponse level, logging to stdout/stderr rather than local disk, no hostPath mounts of /var/log/containers or /var/log/pods, and application-level logging of full prompts, outputs and tool input/output with sensitive data scrubbed first. It does not run any command, targets no specific cluster or fleet, and does not state exclusions.

review-security-k8s-agents-credentials.summary: A repo-level review skill (sub-agent of review-security-k8s-agents-main) for a contributor or review agent reading Kubernetes manifests of AI agent workloads. It is a read-only checklist: authenticated outbound calls must go through an injecting credential proxy or sidecar, the main agent container must not receive Secrets via env, envFrom or volume mounts, no plaintext keys in manifests, automountServiceAccountToken false with the token only in the sidecar, a dedicated non-default serviceAccountName, and no wildcard verbs or resources in RBAC. It names no commands or cluster scope and does not state exclusions.

review-security-k8s-agents-data-exfil.summary: A repo-level review skill (sub-agent of review-security-k8s-agents-main) for a contributor or review agent reading Kubernetes configuration of AI agent workloads. It is a read-only checklist on three fronts: egress NetworkPolicies that must be restrictive with no 0.0.0.0/0 and allowlisted to internal services and the LLM API, outbound routing through an egress gateway or proxy (service mesh, HTTP_PROXY) for inspection and SNI allowlisting, and RBAC or volume mounts that give broad get/list/watch on secrets and configmaps. It names no commands or cluster scope and does not state exclusions; its egress checks overlap with review-security-k8s-agents-firewall.

review-security-k8s-agents-firewall.summary: A repo-level review skill (sub-agent of review-security-k8s-agents-main) for a contributor or review agent reading NetworkPolicies and firewall configuration for AI agent control loops and execution sandboxes. Read-only checklist: default-deny egress with a minimal allowlist, blocking agent access to internal cluster APIs and the cloud metadata address 169.254.169.254 on its credential ports (TCP 80 pre-NAT, 988 post-NAT) while leaving port 53 open for Cloud DNS for GKE, flagging 0.0.0.0/0 egress, restricting ingress to trusted upstreams, and flagging LoadBalancer or NodePort exposure without ingress NetworkPolicies. It names no commands or cluster scope; the only stated exclusion is that port 53 to the metadata address is not flagged.

review-security-k8s-agents-main.summary: A repo-level orchestration skill for a contributor or review agent; it is itself a sub-agent of review-security-k8s-main. It takes the project context produced by review-security-k8s-understand, launches six sub-skills in parallel (sandbox, firewall, credentials, prompt-injection, data-exfil, audit-logs), requires each to return a fixed JSON findings shape, triages findings against the context (for example dropping egress-proxy findings for an air-gapped sandbox, or root-in-sandbox findings when a gVisor or Kata RuntimeClass is confirmed) and merges them into one JSON array. It performs no checks of its own, runs no commands, and does not state exclusions.

review-security-k8s-agents-prompt-inject.summary: A repo-level review skill (sub-agent of review-security-k8s-agents-main) for a contributor or review agent reading AI agent deployment configuration. It is read-only and holds only two checks: require an LLM-specific API gateway or WAF sidecar and flag raw agent APIs exposed to untrusted traffic, and ensure system prompts or safety instructions kept in ConfigMaps or environment variables cannot be altered by less privileged workloads. It names no commands or cluster scope and does not state exclusions; despite the description it has no input-sanitization check.

review-security-k8s-agents-sandbox.summary: A repo-level review skill (under .agents/skills, run by a reviewing agent against manifests in a pull request or a cluster, read-only) that audits the execution sandboxes an LLM agent uses to run untrusted code (Python REPLs, bash tools, WASM). It checks three things: a hardened RuntimeClass (gVisor or Kata) instead of a standard pod, separation of the sandbox from the main agent loop plus restrictive seccomp/AppArmor profiles, and ephemeral lifecycles with low CPU, memory and ephemeral-storage limits. It is one of six sub-skills launched by review-security-k8s-agents-main and does not state exclusions.

review-security-k8s-gateway.summary: A repo-level review skill (under .agents/skills, read-only, run against manifests in a pull request or a cluster) that audits Kubernetes Gateway API objects: Gateway, HTTPRoute, TCPRoute, TLSRoute and ReferenceGrant. It flags overlapping hostnames or paths that let one route hijack another, cross-namespace route or secret references without a narrow ReferenceGrant, weak TLS listener settings, missing allowedRoutes namespace restrictions, and wildcard or overly broad hostnames. It is one of ten sub-skills launched by review-security-k8s-main; it covers Gateway API only (classic Ingress is left to review-security-k8s-network) and does not state exclusions.

review-security-k8s-main.summary: A repo-level orchestrator skill (under .agents/skills, read-only) that runs a general Kubernetes security review: it first invokes review-security-k8s-understand for project context, then launches ten sub-skills in parallel (rbac, nodes, network, gateway, namespaces, service-accounts, storage, admission, pod, and agents-main), each told to emit a fixed JSON findings schema with agent, message, file and line. It then triages the raw findings against the context (for example dropping hostPath warnings for CSI daemonsets, or downgrading NetworkPolicy warnings when a strict service mesh exists) and merges them into one JSON array. It performs no checks itself and does not state exclusions.

review-security-k8s-namespaces.summary: A repo-level review skill (under .agents/skills, read-only, run against manifests in a pull request or a cluster) that audits how namespaces are used as isolation boundaries. It flags most workloads piled into one namespace, mixing of trust levels or tenants, custom workloads in default/kube-system/kube-public/kube-node-lease, namespace names that impersonate system components, labels or annotations that bypass policy (OPA exemptions, pod-security enforce=privileged), absurd ResourceQuotas or LimitRanges, suspicious namespace finalizers, cross-namespace references without ReferenceGrant or via ExternalName, and leftover Secrets, ServiceAccounts or RoleBindings in namespaces with no pods. It is a sub-skill of review-security-k8s-main and does not state exclusions.

review-security-k8s-network.summary: A repo-level review skill (under .agents/skills, read-only, run against manifests in a pull request or a cluster) that audits Kubernetes network isolation and exposure: NetworkPolicies, Services, Ingresses and service mesh policy. It requires default-deny ingress and egress NetworkPolicies per namespace, flags missing egress limits and broad CIDRs or empty selectors, flags public LoadBalancers, NodePort services and exposed admin ports (22, 3389, 2379, 10250), requires TLS and HTTPS redirects on Ingress, flags hand-written Endpoints/EndpointSlices and hostNetwork: true, and for Istio-style meshes requires STRICT PeerAuthentication and default-deny AuthorizationPolicies. It is a sub-skill of review-security-k8s-main; Gateway API objects are left to review-security-k8s-gateway, and it does not state exclusions.

review-security-k8s-nodes.summary: A repo-level review skill (under .agents/skills, read-only, run against manifests in a pull request or a cluster) that audits ways a compromised pod or node could escalate to cluster-wide control. It flags hostPath mounts of kubelet credentials (/etc/kubernetes, /var/lib/kubelet, kubeconfig) and of container runtime sockets (docker.sock, containerd.sock), extra RBAC bindings for system:nodes or system:node:<name> that bypass NodeRestriction, roles granting impersonate on system:nodes, service-account roles that can create/update/patch/delete nodes or nodes/status, and broad tolerations (operator: Exists with no key) that let untrusted workloads land on control-plane nodes. It recommends ValidatingAdmissionPolicies as the fix for hostPath abuse. It is a sub-skill of review-security-k8s-main and does not state exclusions.

review-security-k8s-pod.summary: Repo-level review skill (run by a contributor or by the review-security-k8s-main orchestrator) that reads Pod specs and their PodSecurityContext/SecurityContext and flags: privileged, host namespaces (hostNetwork/hostPID/hostIPC/hostUsers), hostPath volumes, allowPrivilegeEscalation, root execution, added capabilities, missing capabilities.drop ALL, missing readOnlyRootFilesystem and seccomp, use of the default ServiceAccount, token automounting, Secret-based SA tokens, and images not pinned by digest. Read-only manifest review, cluster-agnostic, single resource type (Pods and pod templates). Does not state exclusions, though it does not cover RBAC, network, or storage settings beyond hostPath.

review-security-k8s-rbac.summary: Repo-level review skill (contributor or review-security-k8s-main orchestrator) that reads Role, ClusterRole, RoleBinding and ClusterRoleBinding manifests and flags: bindings to system:anonymous/unauthenticated/authenticated/masters and system:serviceaccounts groups, cluster-admin grants, write access to system: bindings, escalation paths (bind/escalate/impersonate, writes to rbac.authorization.k8s.io, CSRs, webhooks, CRDs, tokenreviews, namespaces, networkpolicies), wildcards, deletecollection, over-scoped ClusterRoleBindings, self-modification, and access to secrets, pods/exec, pods/portforward, pods/attach, nodes/proxy, ephemeralcontainers and status subresources. Ships resources/gke-rbac.md, a copy of the GKE RBAC best-practices page with kubectl/jq detection commands and the gcloud --no-enable-insecure-binding-system-* flags. Read-only manifest review, single cluster, GKE-flavoured. Does not state exclusions.

review-security-k8s-service-accounts.summary: Repo-level review skill (contributor or review-security-k8s-main orchestrator) that reads ServiceAccount objects and their bindings and flags: RBAC bound to the default ServiceAccount, one ServiceAccount shared by several apps, automountServiceAccountToken not set to false on the ServiceAccount, several workloads mapped to one GCP identity through the iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account Workload Identity annotation, long-lived kubernetes.io/service-account-token Secrets, imagePullSecrets with broad registry access, and ServiceAccounts with bindings but no workloads. Read-only manifest review, single cluster. Does not state exclusions; RBAC rule content and Pod-level security contexts are covered by sibling skills, not here.

review-security-k8s-storage.summary: Repo-level review skill (contributor or review-security-k8s-main orchestrator) that reads StorageClass, PersistentVolume, PersistentVolumeClaim, volume and volumeMount definitions and flags: writable mounts missing readOnly, subPath on user-writable volumes, hostPath use (recommends local PVs), missing fsGroup, ReadWriteMany access mode, StorageClasses without encryption at rest (CMEK or encrypted parameter), Recycle and unmanaged Retain reclaim policies, allowVolumeExpansion without ResourceQuotas, and CSI Secrets Store mounts without strict limits. Read-only manifest review, single cluster, cloud-agnostic. Does not state exclusions.

review-security-k8s-understand.summary: Repo-level context-building skill run first by the review-security-k8s-main and review-security-k8s-agents-main orchestrators (and cited in docs/architecture/03-security-model.md). It reads the target project's README, diagrams and architecture docs, names the main components and workloads, labels each workload Infrastructure (CSI drivers, ingress controllers) or Application (APIs, databases), and records global compensating controls such as a service mesh enforcing mTLS or cluster-wide OPA/Gatekeeper policies. Output is a short summary that the orchestrators use to triage sub-reviewer findings. Read-only, no checks of its own; it explicitly leaves specific security reviews to the specialized skills.

skill-review.summary: Repo-level skill for a contributor reviewing SKILL.md files in this repository. It checks frontmatter (description opens with the user's action and names its object; YAML-safe values), structure (top-level # Task and # Checks or # Workflow sections, terse headers), prose (no persona setup, no filler, imperative bullets starting with Flag/Require/Ensure) and formatting (single-sentence rules, no loss of checks or domain knowledge when shortening). AGENTS.md and .agents/rules/documentation.md point to it as the style owner for SKILL.md files. Read-only review of skill text; it does not cover placement by persona or whether a skill's checks are correct.

uninstall-kube-agents.summary: Repo-level lifecycle skill for a human or agent operator tearing down a kube-agents install. It gives the release-pinned `curl ... uninstall.sh | bash -s -- --non-interactive --gcp-project-id --gke-cluster-name --gcp-region` one-liner, explains that the engine is `lifecycle.sh destroy` in terraform/examples/full-install against the GCS Terraform state, covers `--source-ref` for pre-Terraform installs, the `terraform`/`helm` prerequisites, the exit-code contract (3 = nothing to remove, 1 = failure) and the JSON report at /tmp/kube-agents-uninstall-report.json. It is a GCP-project-and-cluster-wide write operation (destroys Terraform-owned resources, Helm releases, the PlatformAgent CR, backups) and does not state exclusions beyond pointing at `--help` and the site uninstall page.

upgrade-kube-agents.summary: Repo-level lifecycle skill for upgrading an existing kube-agents install with `upgrade.sh`, either curl-piped at a release tag or from a release bundle. It covers the three `--upgrade-mode` values (harness = one `helm upgrade` re-tagging agent, sandbox and plugin images; operator = CRDs plus operator image; full = CRDs plus a `terraform apply` from install.env), `--drop-undeclared-values`, `--dry-run` versus `--plan`, `--image-tag` versus `--keep-image-tag`, how a baked release version changes flag behaviour, and the JSON report at /tmp/kube-agents-upgrade-report.json. It writes to the cluster and GCP project; it does not cover fresh installs or uninstalls and says installs without a `kube-agents` Helm release must use their own release's script.

a2a-topics.summary: Platform Agent skill (shipped only on a `next`-mode install with the A2A bus) for the `a2a topics list|read|write` CLI: discover provisioned topics and their class (state vs journal), read standing state such as `upgrade-readiness` while relaying provenance and treating exit 2 as 'empty', write topics the profile owns with `--text`/`--data` and task/context/correlation ids, and append dated findings to the shared `annotations` journal. Read and write, fleet-level shared state. It explicitly excludes task status (stream replay), private memory, scratch notes, topics not in `a2a topics list`, and installs without `NATS_URL` or where the shell sandbox has no `a2a` binary.

gke-stockout-investigator.summary: Platform Agent plugin skill (installed into the `platform` profile via the gke-stockout-investigator AgentPlugin) that handles a GKE autoscaler stockout alert from Pub/Sub end to end: send a `send_notification`, check for an open PR on `platform-agent/remediate-stockout-<workload>` with `vcs.py proposal list --source`, confirm the stockout is live via `kubectl get/describe pod`, take a GitOps working copy with `submit_suggestion.py prepare`, run quota/reservation/`kubectl top`/`gcloud beta compute advice capacity[-history]`/`cluster-autoscaler-status` diagnostics, apply eight ComputeClass debugging rules (A-H), edit ComputeClass or workload YAML with remediation comments, commit, and open the PR with `submit_suggestion.py submit --body-file`. Fleet-facing but one alert and one cluster per run; GitOps write, never a live-cluster mutation. It explicitly forbids `execute_code`, forge CLIs, `git add .`, `--body`, and branch-name suffixes.

gke-observability (agents/cluster/skills.summary: Cluster Agent skill with nine short workflows on one GKE cluster: audit logging/monitoring config with `gcloud container clusters describe`, enable Managed Service for Prometheus, check workload logs with `kubectl logs`, recommend dashboards/alerts, OpenTelemetry tracing and Cloud Profiler, two LQL query examples, enable control-plane metrics, and enable Dataplane V2 observability. Three of the workflows are `gcloud container clusters update` writes; the rest are read-only or advisory. It does not state exclusions. A separate, longer `gke-observability` skill exists under agents/platform/skills.

gke-reliability (agents/cluster/skills/g.summary: Cluster Agent skill with six short workflows on one GKE cluster: check regional/multi-zonal layout via `gcloud container clusters describe --format=json(location, locations)`, list PDBs with `kubectl get pdb` plus an example PDB manifest, grep a Deployment for liveness/readiness/startup probes, a note on SIGTERM and `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`, an example `topologySpreadConstraints` block, and a `gcloud container clusters update --maintenance-window-*` command. Mostly read-only checks and example manifests the agent can propose; the maintenance-window step is a cluster write. It does not state exclusions. A separate, longer `gke-reliability` skill exists under agents/platform/skills.

gke-stall-detection.summary: Cluster Agent, read-only, single cluster and one namespace (or one kind in it). Runs /opt/data/scripts/stall_report.py (agents/platform/scripts/stall_report.py), which applies four heuristics (generation-lag, stale-condition, repeating-warnings, dangling-reference) over kubectl get output for Gateways, HTTPRoutes, Deployments, custom resources and other namespaced kinds, with age thresholds and --kind/--threshold-minutes/--json flags, then records the finding on the kanban card via kanban_complete (including the Session KV controller-stall card format). It explicitly excludes failing-pod and bad-event symptoms (those go to gke-workload-troubleshooting and gke-reliability), never patches, opens PRs or reads Secret contents, and notes that Secret-typed references are unchecked under the default read-only identity.

gke-storage (agents/cluster/skills/gke-s.summary: A short how-to on configuring GKE storage: writing a StorageClass for the Persistent Disk CSI driver, choosing between the PD, Filestore and Cloud Storage FUSE CSI drivers, creating a ReadWriteMany PVC, and expanding a volume by editing the PVC. Every workflow is a create-or-apply write and there are no diagnostic commands, so it reads as configuration guidance rather than single-cluster debugging. Sits under the Cluster Agent; a longer upstream-synced copy with the same name lives under agents/platform/skills. Does not state exclusions.

gke-workload-scaling (agents/cluster/ski.summary: Workflows for scaling GKE workloads: kubectl scale for manual replicas, kubectl autoscale and an HPA manifest (assets/hpa-example.yaml, CPU and memory targets), a VPA manifest (assets/vpa-example.yaml) with update modes including InPlaceOrRecreate, enabling VPA and node-pool Cluster Autoscaler with gcloud container clusters update, and best practices on requests, HPA/VPA metric conflicts, PDBs and the HPA stabilization window. All commands are writes to one cluster; there are no commands for reading HPA or VPA status. Sits under the Cluster Agent; an upstream-synced copy with a capacity-obtainability footer lives under agents/platform/skills. Does not state exclusions.

gke-workload-security (agents/cluster/sk.summary: Workflows for auditing and hardening one GKE cluster: a read-only audit script (scripts/audit_cluster.sh, gcloud container clusters describe for Workload Identity, Network Policy or Dataplane V2, Shielded Nodes, Binary Authorization, private nodes), then write steps for Workload Identity binding (kubectl create, gcloud iam add-iam-policy-binding, kubectl annotate, a test pod asset), enabling Calico network policy in two gcloud steps, a default-deny NetworkPolicy asset, Shielded Nodes, GKE Sandbox, Pod Security Standards labels, a Secret Manager CSI SecretProviderClass and Dataplane V2 NetworkLogging. Only the audit and the describe check are read-only; the rest mutates cluster or IAM state. Sits under the Cluster Agent; a longer upstream-synced copy lives under agents/platform/skills. Does not state exclusions.

gke-workload-troubleshooting (agents/clu.summary: Cluster Agent, read-only, single workload in one namespace. A five-step SOP: acquire project, cluster, workload and a one-hour time window; read pod and Deployment status and classify Pending, CrashLoopBackOff (exit 137 vs other), ContainerCreating; read namespace events with kubectl get events or gcloud logging read and match FailedScheduling, FailedMount, image-pull failures (with a git log search for the last working tag); read current and previous container logs for OOM, stack traces, egress timeouts and read-only-filesystem errors; check Service endpoints and NetworkPolicies; then record the RCA and a proposed YAML patch on the kanban card with kanban_complete. It explicitly excludes applying patches, opening PRs (submit-suggestion is the Platform Agent's) and passing findings through the chat reply.

capacity-obtainability.summary: Platform Agent, read-only diagnosis and design, project and region scope rather than one cluster. Checks regional quota (gcloud compute regions describe), reservations, live node and pod usage (kubectl top), Spot and Flex-Start obtainability (gcloud beta compute advice capacity, capacity-history) across zones, and future reservation windows for deadline-bound TPU or VM batch jobs (gcloud beta compute advice calendar-mode); records each check with record_evidence (or an Evidence section when the tool is absent), attaches ComputeClass, NAP, ProvisioningRequest and Kueue LocalQueue manifests with attach_artifact, requires a three-path On-Demand/Spot/Flex-Start report, and lists eight ComputeClass resilience rules (fallbacks, large shapes, disk generation mix, On-Demand floor, regional scarcity, quota exceeded, priority starvation, Hyperdisk compatibility). It explicitly excludes creating clusters, applying manifests, opening PRs and handling inbound stockout alerts, which it sends to the gke-stockout-investigator plugin skill.

cluster-agent-lifecycle.summary: Platform Agent skill for the lifecycle of per-cluster Cluster Agent Hermes profiles: create one at cluster onboarding and delete one at teardown with agents/platform/scripts/cluster_agent_profile.py (create/delete, --project --cluster --location), resolve a profile with the get_cluster_profile_name and list_cluster_profiles tools, and delegate any single-cluster runtime debugging task (crash loops, OOMs, scheduling, mounts, connectivity, autoscaling, storage) to that profile through a kanban card (kanban_create, kanban_show, kanban_complete), including a multi-cluster fan-out pattern. It also describes the hourly cluster-agent-reconcile cron job (cluster_agent_reconcile.py, --dry-run, --require-create-pass) that creates and prunes profiles across every project in scope, with its fleet_scope.json snapshot and two-clean-run prune rule. It writes profiles on the data PVC but is read-only against clusters; it explicitly excludes debugging tenant workloads directly, opening pull requests (that is submit-suggestion), and repairing the roster from other work.

fleet-audit.summary: Platform Agent skill that turns the findings of the nine autonomous fleet audit streams into one continuously rewritten ledger issue per stream on the GitOps repository's forge (GitHub or GitLab) and into narrow remediation pull requests, through audit_report.py (start, finish, draft, list, grep, fetch, remediate). The streams it covers are compliance-audit (security and RBAC posture), security-patch-orchestrator (upgrade and patch readiness), obtainability-audit (workload reliability), fleet-wide-cost-analysis (fleet waste), fleet-consistency-drift, ai-security-audit (AI workload security), stockout-prevention (capacity), gcp-networking-fabric-audit (VPC and IPAM) and gce-compute-fleet-audit (GCE VMs and MIGs); the folder ships the collectors collect.py (compliance, obtainability, AI security), fleet_drift.py, fleet_waste.py, fleet_stockout.py and patch_readiness.py, plus the report store reader report_status.py. It defines the findings.json contract (scope.clusters with checks_run per check, checks_not_applicable, limitations, skipped, findings with evidence and a three-part recommendation, declared postures, resolved_because), the collector-manifest cross-check, partial and held runs, the silent_ok rule, the /remediate protocol, and the three request forms (run a stream per its SOP as a worker, trigger the cron job with hermes cron run, or answer from past reports). The agent is read-only against clusters and GCP; all git and forge writes are the script's. It explicitly excludes hand-written issues, bodies or timestamps, opening a second ledger, reopening merged PRs, deleting branches, running the audit inline when asked to trigger the cron job, and answering questions about past runs (that is fleet-audit-reports).

fleet-audit-reports.summary: Platform Agent skill for answering questions about past fleet audit runs from the on-pod report store at /opt/data/fleet-audit/reports/<audit-id>/<owner>/<name>/ (latest.json plus a 14-run ring), using report_query.py subcommands streams, show, findings, finding, checks, diff and runs, with --repo, --run, --severity, --cluster, --check and --limit filters. It covers what a stream last found, open critical counts, what changed between two runs, which clusters were skipped or partly covered, held-open and partial ledgers, and when each stream last ran (liveness never/completed/running/died/error). Read-only, fleet-wide, no cluster or forge access. It explicitly excludes running, publishing or remediating an audit (fleet-audit owns those), opening store files directly, acting on a running or died lease, and treating a missing or unreadable record as a clean fleet.

fleet-upgrade-verification.summary: Platform Agent skill that reports every GKE cluster's control-plane and lowest node-pool version against a target version or the cluster's release-channel default (fleet_upgrade_report.py: --project, --target-version, --output, --state-dir, --rollout-in-progress, --readiness, --at, --kubeconfig-dir), grading members lagging/patch-behind/current/ahead/unknown, tracking rollout progress across runs (completed/started/unchanged/stalled/new) from a record under /opt/data/state/fleet-upgrade-verification/, and with --readiness grading drain-blocking PodDisruptionBudgets, maintenance exclusions and windows, and node-pool skew. A second script, api_deprecation_scan.py (--versions, --target-version, --repo, --manifests-dir, --lease, --output), scans the managed GitOps repositories for apiVersions the target removes, from a removed_apis.json table covering Kubernetes 1.16 through 1.32. Read-only against GCP (gcloud container clusters list, get-server-config, get-credentials), clusters (one kubectl get per member) and Git, fleet-wide. It explicitly excludes upgrade plans and runbooks (gke-upgrades), configuration drift, running the upgrade or the manifest migrations, rendering Helm or Kustomize, deleting exclusions, running gcloud recommender insights, and citing CVE identifiers.

gce-compute-fleet-audit.summary: Platform Agent skill for the gce-compute-fleet-audit stream: run the collector compute_fleet_audit.py (optional --project-id and --output) over the target GCP projects with gcloud compute reads, then evaluate its manifest against governance/gce_compute_fleet_sop.md and hand the result to the fleet-audit harness with start and finish --manifest-file. Its four collector-verified checks are gce-startup-script-status (serial console boot and startup-script failures), mig-convergence-stalled (MIG resize loops), sole-tenant-headroom (node groups at capacity) and orphaned-snapshots (snapshots of deleted disks older than 90 days). Read-only, project-scoped rather than cluster-scoped, fleet-wide. It explicitly excludes ops-agent-guest-health, which is off the roster, and hand-running any check.

gcp-config-connector.summary: Platform Agent skill that authors Config Connector (KCC) v1beta1 manifests for Google Cloud resource changes and submits them as a pull request through submit-suggestion (prepare and submit on branch platform-agent/kcc-<kind>-<name>) under clusters/<cluster>/provisioning/. It covers ContainerCluster and ContainerNodePool changes (grow, autoscale, release channel, adopt), SQLInstance changes (read replica, tier, backups), and ComputeFirewall rules, with a read-only create/acquire/edit decision from kubectl get, kubectl auth can-i and gcloud describe, mandatory deletion-policy: abandon and state-into-spec: absent annotations, immutable-field catalogues per kind in references/, and validation with kubectl explain. GitOps-write via PR only; never applies. It explicitly excludes Kubernetes workload manifests (gke-manifest-generation), imperative cluster creation (gke-cluster-creation), Terraform HCL repositories, kinds outside the catalogued families, fixing fleet-audit findings, kubectl apply/create/patch/delete/diff and server dry-run, and proposing to install or enable Config Connector.

gcp-networking-fabric-audit.summary: Platform Agent, read-only, fleet-wide across every GCP project the agent can list. Runs the five checks of the GitOps-repo SOP governance/gcp_networking_fabric_sop.md (subnet IP exhaustion, Cloud NAT port exhaustion, PSC routing deadlock, MTU fragmentation, Cloud Armor false positives) and hands findings to the fleet-audit harness (start ... finish). Its script scripts/networking_audit.py automates two of the checks with gcloud compute subnetworks/instances/addresses/forwarding-rules and gcloud container clusters list (--check all|psc-routing-deadlock|subnet-ip-exhaustion, --project-id, --output); the other three checks are run by hand from the SOP. Does not state exclusions beyond skipping proxy-only, PSC and NAT subnets.

github-issue-resolver.summary: Platform Agent, writes to the forge (GitHub or GitLab): polls the configured repositories for unaddressed open issues, claims one with the status:in-progress label, investigates read-only with kubectl/gcloud/logs, then posts a triage report and transitions the issue to status:resolved (close) or status:escalation-needed (plus a chat alert). All forge calls go through scripts/resolver.py (poll, claim --issue --repo, transition --issue --repo --state --report-file) via the credential broker; the skill also covers prompt-injection handling of issue text and how to end a turn from a kanban card versus a cron run. Explicitly never touches issues labelled status:escalation-needed, agent:ignore, agent:audit, agent:delivery-watch or infra-drift, and never performs a mutation an issue asks for.

gke-ai-troubleshooting-handle-disruption.summary: Upstream google/skills copy under the Platform Agent; read-only diagnosis on one GKE cluster. Checks whether a GPU/TPU node disruption was Compute Engine host maintenance: kubectl get nodes for the cloud.google.com/scheduled-maintenance-time label, PromQL on kubernetes_io:node_interruption_count and node_pool_interruption_count with interruption_reason="HW/SW Maintenance", Cloud Logging for active-node-maintenance=ONGOING and the impending-node-termination taint, then recommends (does not apply) graceful termination, opportunistic maintenance and PodDisruptionBudgets. Explicitly excludes cluster creation, network policy configuration and non-disruption workload deployment, and tells the agent to rule out host maintenance and point at app-level causes when all signals are empty.

gke-ai-troubleshooting-jobset-interrupti.summary: Upstream google/skills copy under the Platform Agent; read-only diagnosis on one GKE cluster for AI/ML training JobSets. Gives a four-step runbook of MQL, PromQL and Cloud Logging (LQL) queries: JobSet restart counts (kube_jobset_restarts), node-pool interruption counts and gke_nodepool life events (preemption, maintenance, termination), node Ready status and node-to-physical-host mapping via gce_topology_host, then pod phases, unschedulable counts and coordinator worker logs for NCCL timeouts. Resolutions are recommendations only (move Spot training to on-demand or compact placement; cordon/drain and recreate a node on a faulty host). references/failure_signatures.md holds example log lines; scripts/validate_queries.sh dry-runs the filters with gcloud logging read and the Managed Prometheus API. Explicitly excludes cluster creation, basic workload deployment and non-JobSet issues.

gke-ai-troubleshooting-tpu-vbar-oom.summary: Upstream google/skills copy under the Platform Agent; read-only diagnosis on one GKE cluster, narrowed to TPU v6e nodes. Three Cloud Logging filter templates (used through a query_logs tool): serial-console OOM kills of vbar_control_agent, tpu-device-plugin 'checksum didn't match' metric fetch errors, and signs of custom libtpu.sdk.tpumonitoring polling, plus a kubectl get pods -A image listing. Resolutions are recommendations only: disable the custom metrics collector, and upgrade GKE when the resilient agent ships. references/failure_signatures.md holds example log lines; scripts/validate_queries.sh dry-runs two filters with gcloud logging read. Explicitly excludes non-TPU container OOMs and standard node lifecycle operations.

gke-app-onboarding.summary: Upstream google/skills copy under the Platform Agent; a write path for one cluster. Covers first-time onboarding of an application to GKE: assess the app, write a Dockerfile (or use Cloud Native Buildpacks), build and push to Artifact Registry (gcloud auth configure-docker, docker build/push, gcloud artifacts docker images describe --show-package-vulnerability), generate a Deployment plus ClusterIP Service manifest with probes and resource limits, then deploy with the GKE MCP tools apply_k8s_manifest / get_k8s_rollout_status / get_k8s_resource or kubectl apply as fallback. assets/ holds a sample Node.js app (Dockerfile, index.js, package.json) and a hardened deployment.yaml that SKILL.md itself does not reference. Explicitly excludes general cluster administration and upgrades, pointing to gke-basics and gke-upgrades, and defers autoscaling, observability, security and reliability to other gke-* skills.

gke-backup-dr.summary: Platform Agent skill for Backup for GKE. It gives the gcloud beta container backup-restore commands to enable the BackupRestore addon, create backup plans (with --include-volume-data, --include-secrets, retention, cron or RPO schedules, CMEK), trigger manual backups, create restore plans and run and verify restores. It is a write skill on one GKE cluster at a time, with restore-safety rules on conflict policies and a rule to confirm before restoring into production. It explicitly does not cover database backups and does not cover the broader Google Cloud Backup and DR service.

gke-basics.summary: Platform Agent entry skill for core GKE work: choosing Autopilot vs Standard, private-cluster flags, Workload Identity annotation, Autopilot CPU rounding, and fetching cluster credentials into a per-target KUBECONFIG. The references add a tool-preference order (Developer Knowledge MCP for facts; GKE MCP tools, then gcloud, then kubectl for cluster operations), a table of 23 GKE MCP tools with gcloud and kubectl fallbacks for cluster, node pool, resource, log and operation actions, Terraform and client-library snippets, and an error table. It covers both read and write actions on single clusters. It explicitly excludes GKE networking (gke-networking), security hardening (gke-platform-security, gke-workload-security) and upgrades (gke-upgrades), and points to gke-cluster-creation for cluster architecture.

gke-batch-hpc.summary: Platform Agent skill for running batch and HPC work on GKE. It gives manifests for Kubernetes Jobs, JobSet, Kueue ClusterQueue and LocalQueue, and Kubeflow MPIJob, the kubectl install lines for Kueue and the MPI Operator, a gcloud node-pools create command for compact placement on Standard clusters, and cost rules (Spot via ComputeClass, scale-to-zero, backoffLimit, checkpointing, maintenance exclusions). It writes workloads into a single cluster. A local footer requires loading capacity-obtainability before scheduling GPU/TPU jobs with a deadline. It explicitly excludes standard web application deployments (gke-app-onboarding) and defers Spot-fallback YAML to gke-compute-classes.

gke-cluster-autoscaler.summary: Platform Agent skill for the GKE Cluster Autoscaler, Node Auto Provisioning and node pool auto-creation. It covers enabling autoscaling (gcloud node-pools and clusters update flags), tuning (autoscaling profiles, location policy, consolidation delay), reading cluster-autoscaler-visibility logs, and diagnosing scale-up failures (stockouts, quota, IP exhaustion, cooldown cascade) and scale-down blockers, with two scripts (log-autoscaler-events.sh tails Cloud Logging; find-scale-down-blockers.sh scans pods, PDBs and nodes with kubectl) and a CapacityBuffer example. It mixes read-only diagnosis with cluster-level write commands on a single cluster. It explicitly defers ComputeClass YAML, schemas and priority configuration to gke-compute-classes.

gke-cluster-creation.summary: Platform Agent provisioning skill that creates GKE clusters from five templates (golden-path Autopilot, Autopilot dev/test, Standard regional, L4 GPU inference, A3 Hypercompute), each as a gcloud command and a create_cluster MCP payload, with a workflow (discover, gather inputs, choose mode, confirm, create, track with get_operation, verify with get_cluster) and rules to warn about Standard mode, Day-0 choices, cost and quota. Local footers require creating the Cluster Agent profile (python3 /opt/data/scripts/cluster_agent_profile.py create) right after creation, deleting it at teardown, and loading capacity-obtainability before recommending GPU/TPU capacity. It is a write skill at project scope. It explicitly excludes application onboarding and deployment configuration (gke-app-onboarding).

gke-compute-classes.summary: Platform Agent skill for authoring, tuning and debugging GKE ComputeClass objects: priorities with Spot, reservation, DWS FlexStart and On-Demand fallbacks, GPU and TPU targeting, machine families, location policy, activeMigration and consolidation, the dynamic-rwo StorageClass for stateful PVs, Autopilot mode on Standard clusters, Karpenter migration, and access control via RBAC plus a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy. It ships fifteen example YAML assets (labelled EXAMPLE TEMPLATE - DO NOT DEPLOY), ten reference files and a copy of log-autoscaler-events.sh identical to the one in gke-cluster-autoscaler. It writes cluster-scoped CRDs on a single cluster. It explicitly excludes cluster-level Node Auto Provisioning configuration and general cluster creation.

gke-cost-analysis.summary: Platform Agent skill (agents/platform/skills, upstream google/skills copy) for answering GKE cost questions. It covers BigQuery billing-export queries with `bq query` (per-workload, per-cluster, per-namespace cost, net vs gross credits), checking that GKE Cost Allocation is enabled, `gcloud billing budgets list`, and live `kubectl top nodes/pods` to compare usage with requests; it explains Autopilot (per-pod-request) vs Standard (per-VM plus management fee) pricing. Scope spans projects and clusters (fleet-wide billing data) and is read-only apart from one `gcloud container clusters update --enable-cost-allocation` snippet; it explicitly excludes applying optimizations, VPA/MPA rightsizing manifests, and ComputeClass selection (deferred to gke-cost-optimization).

gke-cost-optimization.summary: Platform Agent skill (upstream google/skills copy) for reducing GKE cost once waste is known. It covers ResourceQuota manifests, VPA in recommendation mode (`updateMode: Off`) with a P95*1.2 rightsizing rule and MPA, Spot VMs via a `ComputeClass` with fallback or the Autopilot `cloud.google.com/gke-provisioning: Spot` nodeSelector, a machine-family cost table, Committed Use Discounts, stopping idle dev clusters, and dev/test deviations from the golden path. Write-oriented (its examples use `kubectl apply`, which this install routes through the GitOps PR path), single cluster or namespace at a time; it explicitly excludes general ComputeClass provisioning and GPU selection (gke-compute-classes) and billing analysis (gke-cost-analysis).

gke-golden-path.summary: Platform Agent skill (upstream google/skills copy) holding the recommended Autopilot cluster configuration. It lists always-apply defaults (private nodes, Workload Identity, ADVANCED_DATAPATH, Cloud DNS, OPTIMIZE_UTILIZATION, VPA, monitoring/logging components, Secret Manager rotation), customer-configurable settings (DNS endpoint, IPAM, maxPodsPerNode, boot disk, maintenance exclusions), Day-0 vs Day-1 rules, guardrails for auditing an existing cluster against the baseline, and a condensed `assets/golden-path-autopilot.yaml`. It names the `get_cluster`/`create_cluster`/`update_cluster` MCP tools and is a design and audit reference for one cluster at a time; it explicitly excludes workload autoscaling (gke-workload-scaling).

gke-inference.summary: Platform Agent skill (upstream google/skills copy) for serving AI/ML models on GKE. It covers the GKE Inference Quickstart CLI (`gcloud container ai profiles models list`, `profiles list --model`, `profiles manifests create` with `--model-server`, `--accelerator-type`, `--target-ntpot-milliseconds`), reviewing and deploying the generated manifest with `kubectl apply`, a GPU `ComputeClass` for Autopilot, an accelerator selection table (T4 through GB200 and TPU v5e-v7x), an HPA on GPU metrics, vLLM tuning tips, and a troubleshooting table. Single-cluster, write-oriented deployment guidance; it explicitly excludes generic batch and HPC work (gke-batch-hpc).

gke-manifest-generation.summary: Platform Agent skill (upstream google/skills copy with repo-specific substitutions) for writing or editing Kubernetes YAML for GKE Autopilot and Standard. It mandates explicit namespaces, dedicated ServiceAccounts, requests/limits, Spot nodeSelector plus toleration for non-prod, Pod Security Standards hardening, liveness/readiness/startup probes, ClusterIP and Gateway API over Ingress, subPath and StorageClass rules, anti-affinity and PDBs, and stable list keys for server-side apply; references hold full examples for a hardened Nginx Deployment, NetworkPolicy, a vLLM GPU workload with GCS FUSE, and Gateway/HTTPRoute. It directs inference manifests to `gcloud container ai profiles manifests create` on stdout and grounding lookups to `search_documents`/`get_documents`; it is authoring-only (no cluster operations) and explicitly excludes troubleshooting (gke-workload-troubleshooting), cluster provisioning (gke-cluster-creation), and Config Connector manifests (gcp-config-connector).

gke-multitenancy.summary: Platform Agent skill (upstream google/skills copy) for sharing one GKE cluster between teams or environments. It compares namespace-per-team, namespace-per-environment, node-pool-per-team and cluster-per-team models, then gives manifests for namespaces and labels, namespace-scoped Role/RoleBinding to Google Groups, ResourceQuota, LimitRange (with the rule that min/max need defaults), a same-namespace-plus-DNS NetworkPolicy, cost-center labels and `--enable-cost-allocation`. Single-cluster, write-oriented (`kubectl create/label/apply`, `gcloud container clusters update`); it explicitly excludes single-tenant cluster configuration and general deployment steps (gke-basics, gke-app-onboarding) and defers RBAC hardening and default-deny policy to gke-platform-security and gke-workload-security.

gke-networking.summary: Platform Agent reference for core GKE cluster networking, read and write at the cluster level: golden-path settings for private nodes, private endpoint enforcement, DNS endpoint access, Dataplane V2, Cloud DNS, Auto IPAM and max pods per node; get-credentials via --dns-endpoint or --internal-ip; create-auto with a bring-your-own VPC and subnet; Pod and Service CIDR sizing; Cloud NAT egress; and a local footer that checks controlPlaneEndpointsConfig before passing --dns-endpoint and points at /opt/data/scripts/gke_endpoint.py. Uses MCP get_cluster, update_cluster, apply_k8s_manifest, get_k8s_resource plus gcloud. Explicitly excludes application ingress, load balancing and service networking (gke-service-networking) and defers NetworkPolicy manifests to gke-workload-security and gke-multitenancy.

gke-observability (agents/platform/skill.summary: Platform Agent reference for GKE monitoring and logging on a single cluster, mostly write: golden-path loggingConfig and monitoringConfig components including APISERVER, SCHEDULER and CONTROLLER_MANAGER, gcloud container clusters update --monitoring / --enable-managed-prometheus / --enable-dataplane-v2-flow-observability, kubectl top for live usage, gcloud logging read and LQL queries for system, workload and audit logs, key metrics, an alert threshold table with Cloud Monitoring rules, node-health metrics, cost notes and a pointer to Cloud Trace and Profiler. Uses MCP gke:get_cluster, gke:list_k8s_events, gke:get_k8s_logs, gke:get_k8s_cluster_info, gke:describe_k8s_resource. Explicitly excludes application logging frameworks and external APMs outside GKE.

gke-platform-security.summary: Platform Agent reference for cluster-level GKE security hardening, read and write via gcloud and MCP (gke:get_cluster, gke:update_cluster, k8s:check_k8s_auth, k8s:get_k8s_resource, k8s:apply_k8s_manifest): golden-path values for Workload Identity pool, Secret Manager add-on with rotation, insecure RBAC binding config, Shielded Nodes and GKE_METADATA; commands to enable Secret Manager, Binary Authorization, Shielded Nodes and GKE Sandbox on an existing cluster; RBAC audit via check_k8s_auth or kubectl auth can-i; a table of roles/container.* IAM roles; the GKE service agent and node service account; and gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding patterns for GSAs. Explicitly excludes workload-level controls (Workload Identity bindings, SecretProviderClass, Pod Security Standards, NetworkPolicy, gvisor runtimeClassName), deferring to gke-workload-security, and enterprise RBAC planning (gke-multitenancy).

gke-productionize.summary: Platform Agent orchestrator for a production readiness review of a GKE cluster or one or more applications, mostly read-only discovery (gcloud container clusters describe, kubectl get deployment/namespace/pods/hpa/pdb/networkpolicy) followed by mandatory delegation to gke-app-onboarding, gke-workload-scaling, gke-observability, gke-reliability, gke-platform-security, gke-workload-security, gke-backup-dr, gke-service-networking and gke-cost-optimization, ending in a Red/Amber/Green report per area. It asks for user confirmation before state-changing work. Explicitly excludes deep single-domain implementation, which it hands to the domain skills.

gke-reliability (agents/platform/skills/.summary: Platform Agent reference for workload and cluster availability on a single cluster, read and write via MCP (get_cluster, get_k8s_resource, describe_k8s_resource, apply_k8s_manifest, list_k8s_events) with gcloud and kubectl fallbacks: golden-path regional cluster, surge upgrades, auto-repair, auto-upgrade and REGULAR channel; verifying regional control plane and multi-zone nodes; PodDisruptionBudget manifests; liveness, readiness and startup probe YAML with explicit timeouts; SIGTERM handling with preStop sleep; zone and hostname topology spread constraints; and minimum replica counts per workload type. Explicitly excludes disaster recovery and cluster backups (gke-backup-dr) and defers maintenance windows to gke-upgrades.

gke-service-networking.summary: Platform Agent reference for exposing GKE applications, write via Kubernetes manifests on a single cluster: Gateway and HTTPRoute with the gke-l7-global-external-managed class, legacy GKE Ingress with the gce class annotation, Cloud Armor via BackendConfig securityPolicy and the cloud.google.com/backend-config Service annotation, ManagedCertificate for Ingress and Certificate Manager or Secret TLS on a Gateway HTTPS listener, container-native load balancing via the cloud.google.com/neg annotation, and Private Service Connect via ServiceAttachment. No MCP tools or gcloud commands are listed. Explicitly excludes cluster IP planning, Dataplane V2 network policies and node NAT egress (gke-networking).

gke-storage (agents/platform/skills/gke-.summary: Platform Agent skill (upstream google/skills copy) for configuring storage on a single GKE cluster: it lists the golden-path CSI drivers and built-in StorageClasses, gives manifests for a custom regional pd-ssd StorageClass, ReadWriteOnce PVCs, Filestore ReadWriteMany PVCs and a GCS FUSE bucket mount, and shows PVC expansion via kubectl patch or the gke MCP patch_k8s_resource tool. It is a write skill (apply_k8s_manifest, patch) with best-practice guidance and a pointer to gke-backup-dr for PVC backup. It explicitly excludes database administration and replication strategies outside volume provisioning.

gke-tpu-dynamic-slices-monitoring.summary: Platform Agent skill (upstream google/skills copy) for the GKE TPU Dynamic Slices feature on a single cluster: it diagnoses a Slice custom resource with kubectl describe slice and a lifecycle-state table (SliceNotCreated, SliceCreationFailed, ACTIVATING, ACTIVE, ACTIVE_DEGRADED, FAILED, DEACTIVATING, INCOMPLETE), checks single-slice and JobSet multi-slice pod annotations and nodeSelectors, and gives two confirm-first write procedures: removing stuck finalizers with kubectl patch, and disabling the slice controller (gcloud container clusters update --no-enable-slice-controller, delete the slices.accelerator.gke.io CRD, strip node labels). A references file shows example failure conditions. It explicitly excludes generic node pool creation and non-TPU workloads (pointing to gke-basics and gke-cluster-creation).

gke-tpu-metrics-monitoring.summary: Platform Agent skill (upstream google/skills copy), read-only: it monitors GKE TPU containers, nodes and multi-host node pools through Cloud Monitoring system metrics and PromQL. It covers checking the runtime-metrics prerequisites (containerPort 8431, JAX and GKE versions), the accelerator duty_cycle, memory and tensorcore/bandwidth utilization metrics, node status conditions, node pool status and multi-host availability, interruption counts by type and reason, and 7-day MTTR and MTBI calculations, for one cluster or project-wide. A references file lists metric signatures (node unready, node pool error, preemption, host error, low utilization). It explicitly excludes non-TPU workload monitoring and non-metric TPU debugging.

gke-upgrades.summary: Platform Agent skill (upstream google/skills copy with a repo-added footer) for planning, running and troubleshooting GKE control plane and node pool upgrades on Standard and Autopilot clusters. It covers release channels and support lifecycle, maintenance windows and the three exclusion scopes with their day limits and exact gcloud flags, mandatory overrides, surge and blue-green strategy per workload type, GPU/TPU upgrade constraints, pre- and post-upgrade checklists, gcloud and kubectl runbook templates (upgrade, downgrade, maintenance window), and a nine-item stuck-upgrade troubleshooting guide (PDBs, capacity, bare pods, webhooks, PVCs, stockouts, GPU driver regressions). The footer routes fleet-wide version and readiness checks to the fleet-upgrade-verification skill's fleet_upgrade_report.py and api_deprecation_scan.py scripts, which exist in this repo with the cited flags. It is a write skill producing plans and runbooks and issuing gcloud upgrade commands, for one cluster at a time. It explicitly excludes cluster creation, app onboarding, networking setup and security policy configuration.

gke-workload-scaling (agents/platform/sk.summary: Platform Agent skill (upstream google/skills copy with a repo-added footer) for scaling workloads on a single GKE cluster: manual kubectl scale, Horizontal Pod Autoscaler via kubectl autoscale or the bundled autoscaling/v2 manifest, Vertical Pod Autoscaler enablement on Standard clusters and its update modes (Off, Initial, Auto, InPlaceOrRecreate), a VPA manifest, a rightsizing workflow from VPA Off-mode recommendations with a 20% buffer, and HPA/VPA best practices. It explicitly excludes Cluster Autoscaler, static cluster sizing and node machine-type choices.

gke-workload-security (agents/platform/s.summary: Platform Agent skill (upstream google/skills copy with a repo-applied substitution for the network-policy enablement steps) for hardening workloads and namespaces on a single GKE cluster. It covers a read-only cluster posture audit (scripts/audit_cluster.sh checks Workload Identity, network policy or Dataplane V2, Shielded Nodes, Binary Authorization and private nodes via gcloud describe and jq), Workload Identity KSA-to-GSA binding with a test pod manifest, checking and enabling Calico or Dataplane V2 network policy enforcement and applying a default-deny NetworkPolicy, gVisor runtimeClassName, Pod Security Standards namespace labels, Secret Manager CSI SecretProviderClass, and Dataplane V2 NetworkLogging. It is a write skill (gcloud iam bindings, cluster updates, kubectl apply/label). It explicitly excludes control-plane security, RBAC hardening, Binary Authorization, Shielded Nodes and platform add-ons, pointing to gke-platform-security.

gke-workload-troubleshooting (agents/pla.summary: Platform Agent copy (overlaid from google/skills, with an upstream.lock and two local patches) of a five-step runbook for a failing workload on one GKE cluster: read pod and Deployment status with kubectl, read namespace events (kubectl or gcloud logging read), read current and previous container logs, check Service endpoints and NetworkPolicies, then write a root-cause summary and a corrected manifest. Covers CrashLoopBackOff, OOMKilled, ImagePullBackOff, Pending, ContainerCreating, FailedMount, read-only filesystem and egress timeouts, with a dry-run mode that prints the commands when the cluster is unreachable. Diagnostics are read-only; the only write is a GitOps pull request, and only when the request asked for the fix (SOUL.md section 3, item 3). It excludes cluster provisioning, node pool creation and non-Kubernetes Google Cloud services.

inspect-repository.summary: Platform Agent, read-only. Lets the agent read the source of any GitHub or GitLab repository the install can reach, with no local git, through the credential broker: `inspect_repository.py` offers `clone` (copy a tree or `--prefix` into /opt/data/scratch), and `open`/`list`/`grep`/`fetch`/`close` on a broker-side handle, each printing one JSON object. Covers answering questions about code, reading upstream projects and dependencies, and reading the GitOps repository for context. It does not change repositories (that is submit-suggestion or fleet-audit) and it tells the agent not to re-open a repository that fleet-audit or submit-suggestion already handed it.

kube-agents-observability.summary: Platform Agent, read-only, about kube-agents' own install on the management cluster rather than user workloads. Covers checking agent logs and the audit trail under /opt/data/logs, the fluent-bit sidecar and its ConfigMap, listing chat users from Cloud Logging, GMP and LiteLLM token metrics in Cloud Monitoring, OTel collector resolution from `platformagent.status.telemetry` and the hermes_otel plugin config, Cloud Trace latency breakdowns, and the API (8642/8643) and dashboard (9119) ports. Five Python scripts call the Logging, Monitoring and Trace REST APIs with a gcloud ADC token. It does not state exclusions; metrics guidance is LiteLLM-specific with pointers for vLLM and other providers.

manage-cluster.summary: Platform Agent, write to the data PVC only (no cluster mutation). On a user request to manage an existing GKE cluster it resolves project/cluster/location, verifies the cluster with `verify_gke_cluster` or `gcloud container clusters describe`, runs `/opt/data/scripts/cluster_agent_profile.py create --project --cluster --location` to scaffold a read-only Cluster Agent profile, and confirms. It also explains how to stop managing a cluster: delete it (gke-cluster-creation) or add it to `spec.scope.exclude.clusters` on the PlatformAgent (RECONCILE_EXCLUDE still honoured). It does not create clusters and notes that the hourly cluster-agent-reconcile cron would do the same scaffold automatically.

pr-conversation.summary: Platform Agent, reached from a kanban card filed by the github-repo-watcher cron. Covers answering a reviewer on a pull request the agent itself opened (head branch `platform-agent/*`): `pr_conversation.py poll` to read requests and the whole thread with `can_write`/`can_write_known` gates, deciding question vs change request, making a change via submit-suggestion `prepare --branch <head>`/`submit`, confirming the commit landed with `vcs.py proposal view/commits`, then `reply --verify-commit|--no-change` or `refuse`, and ending with `kanban_complete`/`kanban_block`. It explicitly excludes other people's pull requests, changes wider than the branch under review, merging, closing or approving, and pull requests labelled `agent:ignore`.

submit-suggestion.summary: Platform Agent, the GitOps write path for one-off changes: `submit_suggestion.py prepare --repo --branch platform-agent/<change>-<id>` brings down a working copy under /opt/data/scratch/vcs, the agent edits and stages named files, `submit --title --body-file` (or `--keep-description`, optional `--base`) publishes the branch and opens or refreshes the pull or merge request on GitHub or GitLab, with named refusal codes for base and branch conflicts. Step 5 covers addressing review feedback on an existing PR through `vcs.py proposal view --comments` and the same prepare/submit on the PR's branch.
